title: Standardized flow-cytometry-based protocol to simultaneously measure transcription factor levels
protocol: Design flow cytometry panel as needed for both cell surface markers and intranuclear targets.
Assess if the panel allows for clean separation of cellular population(s).
Resolve transcription factor(s) with the panel.
Ensure isotype controls are negative.
Validate appropriate compensation values.
Prepare a worksheet template on the flow cytometer for fluorescent beads.
Gate on FSC-A vs. SSC-A (Gate 1).
Create a histogram of the beads for the channel closest to SSC.
Gating tightly on the main bead peak in the histogram eliminates bead aggregates (Gate 2).
Create additional histograms of each remaining fluorescent parameter.
Evaluate MFI for each fluorescent channel based off Gate 2.
Adjust cytometer voltages/gains until the MFI from Gate 2 matches the Target MFI.
Record beads and apply voltage/gain values to that day’s flow cytometry experiment.
Set the voltages/gains of each channel to that used in step 4, above.
Prepare the beads by adding 2–3 drops to 1 mL 1× PBS or flow cytometer sheath fluid.
Load the beads onto the machine and begin acquiring events with a flow rate of approximately 150–250 events per second.
Create a graph of forward scatter area vs. side scatter area in the cytometer worksheet and draw a gate around the beads (Gate 1).
Change only FSC and SSC voltages to ensure visualization of the beads.
Select the fluorescent channel/detector on the cytometer that is closest to SSC.
Determine the channel closest to SSC based on the cytometer’s configuration.
On the histogram plot for the selected channel, draw a gate around the main bead peak (Gate 2), avoiding smaller side peaks.
Create histogram plots for each remaining fluorescent channel on the cytometer as child graphs from Gate 2.
Evaluate the median fluorescent intensity of each channel based on Gate 2 in a statistics view within the worksheet.
Record 10,000 events.
Record the MFI for each channel following bead acquisition on a worksheet or master document.
Round the target MFI values to the nearest multiple of 50.
Export and save the bead template and channel/detector MFI values.
Load the bead template and a new tube of flow cytometer setup beads daily before sample collection.
Acquire approximately 150–250 events per second for the beads, but do not record them.
Adjust the voltage/gain for the channel closest to SSC until the target MFI is reached when Gate 2 is properly placed.
Adjust the voltages/gains for each remaining channel on the cytometer until the target MFI values are achieved for each channel.
Record 10,000 events.
Titrate a new antibody lot as normal.
Include an additional sample using the current antibody lot at its current titer.
Compare the newly titrated antibody against the previous lot.
Select the titer that matches the fluorescence expression level of the current antibody lot.
Prepare a tube with the current and new flow cytometer beads.
Adjust all voltages to obtain the current MFI target values for each channel using the current bead lot.
Load the new bead lot and record 10,000 events.
Update the target MFI values as needed with those obtained from the new bead lot.
Count viable cells and remove an appropriate volume to obtain the required number of live cells.
Place cells in a 50 mL conical tube and add 5–10 mL flow cytometry staining buffer.
Spin cells at 700 xg (RCF) for 5 min at 4°C.
Decant supernatant.
Re-suspend cell pellet(s) in 300 μL/108 cells of flow cytometry staining buffer.
Add 100 μL/108 cells of Human Fc block, mix well, and place on ice (4°C) for 20 min.
Add 20 mL flow cytometry staining buffer to the sample(s).
Spin cells at 700 xg (RCF) for 5 min at 4°C.
Decant supernatant.
Re-suspend samples at 25x10^6 cells/mL in flow cytometry staining buffer.
Plate 200 μL of cells into appropriate wells of a labeled round-bottom 96-well plate.
Plate approximately 1–5x10^6 cells/well for compensation controls.
Prepare fixable viability dye (FVD) live/dead discrimination dilution according to the manufacturer’s recommended dilution.
Add 1× PBS following the formula: [Number of sample wells + 2] × 100 μL = total volume of 1× PBS.
Spin plate at 700 xg for 3 min at 4°C.
Flick plate quickly once to remove supernatant.
Blot plate on a stack of paper towels while inverted to remove excess liquid.
Re-suspend each sample well in 100 μL FVD solution, mixing the cells well.
Re-suspend the FVD compensation well in 100 μL FVD solution.
Re-suspend all other compensation wells in 100 μL 1× PBS.
Incubate samples protected from light on ice at 4°C for 20 min.
Add 100 μL flow cytometry staining buffer to each well.
Spin plate at 700 xg (RCF) for 3 min at 4°C.
Flick and blot plate to remove supernatant.
Add 100 μL cell-surface staining cocktail to each well as appropriate and mix well.
Re-suspend all compensation wells in 100 μL flow cytometry staining buffer and mix well.
To each appropriate compensation control, add the single antibody for that control and mix well.
Incubate protected from light on ice (4°C) for 30 min.
Add 100 μL flow cytometry staining buffer to each well.
Spin plate at 700 xg (RCF) for 3 min at 4°C.
Flick and blot plate to remove supernatant.
Add 200 μL flow cytometry staining buffer to each well.
Spin plate at 700 xg (RCF) for 3 min at 4°C.
Flick and blot plate to remove supernatant.
Prepare BioLegend True-NuclearTM Transcription Factor Buffer fixation/permeabilization solution fresh, no more than 1 hour prior to use.
Calculate total volume required as [total number of wells (samples and compensation controls) +2] × 500 μL.
Dilute 4× fixation/permeabilization solution 1:4 in the fixation/permeabilization diluent.
Mix the fixation/permeabilization working solution well and keep at 18°C–22°C until use.
Label 5 mL FACS tubes for each sample and compensation control well.
Add 300 μL of the 1× fixation/permeabilization solution to each tube.
Add 200 μL of the 1× fixation/permeabilization working solution to each well of the plate and mix well.
Transfer each well to its appropriately labeled 5 mL FACS tube.
Incubate protected from light at 18°C–22°C for 1 h.
Prepare BioLegend True-NuclearTM Transcription Factor Buffer.
Dilute 10× permeabilization/wash buffer 1:10 in dH2O to make a working solution.
Mix the working permeabilization/wash buffer well and keep at 18°C–22°C.
Spin the sample tubes at 700 ×g (RCF) for 5 min at 18°C–22°C.
Decant tubes by inverting and blot the mouth of the tube on a paper towel to remove residual liquid.
Add 500 μL 1× permeabilization/wash buffer to each tube.
Spin the sample tubes at 700 xg (RCF) for 5 min at 18°C–22°C.
Decant tubes by inverting (do not shake or flick).
Blot the mouth of the tube on a paper towel to remove residual liquid.
Add 500 μL 1× permeabilization/wash buffer to each tube.
Spin the sample tubes at 700 xg (RCF) for 5 min at 18°C–22°C.
Decant tubes by inverting (do not shake or flick).
Blot the mouth of the tube on a paper towel to remove residual liquid.
Prepare intranuclear staining cocktails in the 1× permeabilization/wash buffer.

Add 1× permeabilization/wash buffer and the correct volumes of each transcription factor staining antibody or isotype control to a tube of appropriate size such that each tube will get 250 μL staining cocktail.
Mix well and keep protected from light at 18°C–22°C until use.
Re-suspend the cell pellets in 250 μL of the appropriate staining or isotype control cocktail.
Mix well by pipetting.
Re-suspend the compensation controls in 250 μL 1× permeabilization/wash buffer and add any transcription factor single-stain compensation controls to the appropriate tube(s).
Incubate protected from light at 18°C–22°C for 30 min.
Add 250 μL 1× permeabilization/wash buffer to each tube.
Spin the sample tubes at 700 xg (RCF) for 5 min at 18°C–22°C.
Decant tubes by inverting (do not shake or flick).
Blot the mouth of the tube on a paper towel to remove residual liquid.
Add 500 μL 1× permeabilization/wash buffer to each tube.
Spin the sample tubes at 700 xg (RCF) for 5 min at 18°C–22°C.
Decant tubes by inverting (do not shake or flick).
Blot the mouth of the tube on a paper towel to remove residual liquid.
Re-suspend cell pellets in 400 μL 1% PFA.
Place all tubes on ice (or in the refrigerator, 4°C) and protect from light until flow cytometry analysis.
